tools.name: list_essays
tools.description: List all published essays and fragments: titles, descriptions, prices, and reading URLs. Full text is free for humans at /read/{slug}; machine reads at /essays/{slug} are paid via x402 (USDC on Base).

tools.name: essay_payment_info
tools.description: Get the x402 payment details for one essay (price, network, asset, recipient wallet) so a machine buyer knows how to pay.

tools.name: lexicon_lookup
tools.description: Look up a term in the Penny Press Lexicon (the author's own definitions of his political-economy vocabulary). Returns free metadata — part of speech and the essays where the term appears — plus payment info for the $0.01 full definition.

tools.name: lexicon_snapshot_info
tools.description: Payment details for the Penny Press Lexicon full dataset snapshot ($0.25): every author-defined term with part of speech, definition, verbatim usage example, and source essays, as versioned JSON.

tools.name: common_cents_info
tools.description: Overview of Common Cents, the Penny Press collection of 20 author-curated quotations in five themed clusters: the themes, quote count, and payment info for the $0.01 full machine-readable set.

tools.name: witness_verify
tools.description: Check whether a SHA-256 content hash has been witnessed by LitWit, the Penny Press literary notary. Free. Returns the matching attestation entries (entry id, sequence, timestamp, title) or an empty result.

tools.name: witness_attest_info
tools.description: How to attest a work's fingerprint with LitWit ($0.05): what to submit, what the tamper-evident receipt contains, and the x402 payment details. The service never sees your work — only its hash.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_essays · Private data: essay_payment_info · Public sink: witness_attest_info.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_essays · Private data: essay_payment_info · Public sink: witness_attest_info

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
